title: Grade 11 Physics — Centre of Mass, Momentum & Rotational Motion
description: Centre of mass, angular quantities, torque, moment of inertia
subject: physics

questions.question: The centre of mass of a system is the point where:
options: The entire mass of the system can be considered to be concentrated for translational motion
questions.explanation: Centre of mass (CM): the average position of mass distribution. For external forces, the system behaves as if its entire mass M is at the CM. x_cm = Σmᵢxᵢ / Σmᵢ.

questions.question: Angular velocity (ω) and linear velocity (v) are related by:
questions.explanation: v = ωr. Linear velocity = angular velocity × radius. Unit of ω = rad/s. Similarly: linear acceleration a = αr (α = angular acceleration), arc length s = rθ.

questions.question: Torque (τ) is defined as:
options: r × F = rF sinθ (moment of force)
questions.explanation: Torque τ = r × F (cross product). Magnitude: τ = rF sinθ (θ = angle between r and F). Torque is the rotational equivalent of force. SI unit: N·m.

questions.question: Moment of Inertia (I) is the rotational analog of:
options: Mass (inertia to rotational motion: τ = Iα, analogous to F = ma)
questions.explanation: I = Σmᵢrᵢ² (depends on mass distribution AND distance from axis). Newton's 2nd law for rotation: τ = Iα (analogous to F = ma). More mass farther from axis → larger I.

questions.question: The moment of inertia of a solid sphere about its diameter is:
questions.explanation: I for solid sphere (about diameter) = (2/5)MR². Hollow sphere: (2/3)MR². Solid cylinder (axis): MR²/2. Thin ring (axis through centre, perpendicular to plane): MR².

questions.question: The Law of Conservation of Angular Momentum states that if no external torque acts, angular momentum:
questions.explanation: L = Iω = constant (when τ_net = 0). A spinning skater pulls arms in → I decreases → ω increases (L conserved). Earth's orbit: closer to sun → faster (Kepler's 2nd law = conservation of angular momentum).

questions.question: Rolling without slipping means:
options: The object slides on the surface
The contact point has zero velocity — v_cm = ωR
questions.explanation: Rolling without slipping: v_cm = ωR. The contact point has zero velocity (instantaneously). Total KE = ½mv² + ½Iω² (translational + rotational KE).

questions.question: The Parallel Axis Theorem states: I = I_cm + ?
questions.explanation: Parallel Axis Theorem: I = I_cm + Md². Where I_cm = moment of inertia about axis through CM, d = distance between parallel axes, M = total mass. Always I ≥ I_cm.

questions.question: Angular momentum L = ?
questions.explanation: L = Iω = r × p (cross product of position and linear momentum). SI unit: kg·m²/s. Angular impulse = change in angular momentum: τ × t = ΔL.

questions.question: The centre of mass of two particles m₁ at x₁ and m₂ at x₂ is at:
questions.explanation: x_cm = (m₁x₁ + m₂x₂)/(m₁+m₂). For equal masses: x_cm = (x₁+x₂)/2 (midpoint). The CM is closer to the heavier mass.

questions.question: When a diver pulls their arms and legs close during a somersault, they spin faster because:
options: Angular momentum is conserved: I decreases → ω increases
questions.explanation: Pulling limbs in reduces moment of inertia I. Since L = Iω = constant (no external torque), ω must increase. This is conservation of angular momentum in action.

questions.question: A wheel (I = 2 kg·m²) has angular acceleration 3 rad/s² applied by a torque. The torque is:
Rotational kinetic energy is:
questions.explanation: Rotational KE = ½Iω². Analogous to translational KE = ½mv². Total KE of rolling body = ½mv² + ½Iω².

questions.question: The equations of angular motion (uniform angular acceleration) are analogous to linear equations. Angular: ω = ω₀ + αt, θ = ω₀t + ½αt², ω² = ω₀² + 2αθ. These are used when:
options: Only when circular motion is uniform
When angular acceleration α is constant
When moment of inertia is zero
questions.explanation: Angular equations of motion apply when α (angular acceleration) is constant — perfectly analogous to linear kinematics. They relate ω (angular velocity), α, θ (angular displacement), and t.

questions.question: The moment of inertia of a uniform thin rod (length L, mass M) about one end is:
questions.explanation: Thin rod about one end: I = ML²/3. About centre (perpendicular): I_cm = ML²/12. By parallel axis theorem: I_end = ML²/12 + M(L/2)² = ML²/12 + ML²/4 = ML²/3. ✓
